newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to hold municipal poll in November.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to hold municipal poll in November.

text.p: Qatar will hold its first municipal elections by November, Justice Minister Najeeb Mohammad al-Nuaimi said on Monday.
All Qataris -- including women -- above age 18 will be allowed to vote.
Nuaimi told the official Qatar News Agency he expected "the drafting of the law organising the elections to be completed before the recess of the current Advisory Council session".
"And elections will be held by next November," he said, but gave no details.

The election plan was announced by Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, 47, as a first step toward enlisting public support and developing democracy in his tiny Gulf Arab state. Sheikh Hamad ousted his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, 65 in a bloodless coup in June 1995.
Qatar, with a native population of around 160,000 and a total population of 650,000 including expatriate workers, is the first Arab state in the Gulf region to order municipal elections.
Kuwait has the only elected Arab parliament in the Gulf, but only men can vote. Neighbouring Bahrain experimented with an elected legislature but the emir dissolved it in 1975.

Sixteen of the 21-member Central Municipal Council will be elected and five will be appointed. It will be an "autonomous body" with power to administer municipalities and propose legislation to the council of ministers.
